R374.note: Rejects '/', '\\', and '..' in the filename (flat directory by design) so the false-fallback bypass can't be reached; the extra realpath(dirname()) check is redundant but harmless.

R375.note: Verified in a JDK 26 sandbox: ObjectInputFilter.Config.createFilter with a single classname and no trailing ';!*' leaves non-matching classes UNDECIDED, which ObjectInputStream treats as allowed - an unrelated Serializable class still deserialized successfully through the 'filter', so arbitrary-class instantiation (the exact contract clause) is not blocked.

R376.note: Switches the sink to Blade's escaping {{ }}; nothing in the case pipeline (controller/presenter) actually produces or expects rich HTML, so the contract's 'if rich text is supported' branch does not apply and plain escaping satisfies the stated contract.

R377.note: Decoding into a narrower JobRequest DTO (Command/Priority only) and setting IsAdmin=false server-side matches gob's field-name-based decoding and the stated contract exactly.

R378.note: Confirmed via Java/Node test: a value like 'https:evil.com' has uri.getHost()==null in Java (treated as a safe relative path by the fix) but WHATWG URL parsing used by real browsers normalizes it to https://evil.com/, so the allowlist can be bypassed for scheme-only absolute URIs; the scheme and protocol-relative (//host) checks are otherwise sound.

R379.note: filepath.Base() strips all directory components including '..' and absolute-path prefixes, fully closing the traversal; no change to legitimate single-name uploads.

R380.note: Installed expr-eval's current npm release (2.0.2) and confirmed require('expr-eval') has no top-level 'parse' export (only Parser.parse); the fixed code's `const { parse } = require('expr-eval')` is undefined, so calling parse(expression) throws for every request, including legitimate arithmetic - violating the contract's 'still return JSON with a numeric value' clause and silently breaking the endpoint entirely, which the write-up does not flag.

R381.note: fgets bounds the read, truncation is detected and the remainder is drained before rejecting, and the out_capacity check is preserved - matches the stated contract.

R382.note: encode_entities() on the reported sink correctly neutralizes HTML metacharacters; scope correctly limited to the reported finding (write-up notes the sibling ticket_id issue without silently expanding the fix).

R383.note: Removes verify_signature=False, supplies a server-held secret and explicit algorithms=["HS256"], and adds exp/error handling; standard, correctly-shaped PyJWT fix.

R384.note: Escapes *()\ and NUL to their RFC4515 \xx hex forms before filter construction; correct and complete LDAP metacharacter escaping.

R385.note: Fixed code checks `message.UserId`, but ChatMessage (in the same case bundle) only defines `AuthorUserId` - this is a compile error (no such member), so the patch as written does not build.

R386.note: Replacing the string-built setTimeout argument with a closure callback eliminates code generation entirely while calling recordReminder with identical arguments and timing.

R387.note: Fallback exec now reuses the already-basename()'d $source/$target and wraps both in escapeshellarg(), matching the primary path's protection and the stated return/side-effect contract.

R388.note: Parameterized INSERT via setString(1, param) removes the injection; relies on DatabaseHelper.getSqlStatement(sql) which isn't in the provided files, but the write-up explicitly flags a prepareStatement(sql) fallback if that signature doesn't exist.

R389.note: Straightforward PreparedStatement with '?' placeholder using standard JDBC APIs already imported in the file; resource cleanup extended correctly to include the PreparedStatement.

R390.note: Files.list() is the right replacement for Runtime.exec(dir/ls) and closes the injection cleanly, but the original handleSink never wrote any output to the response at all (no stdout was read or forwarded) - the fix adds new response.getWriter() output that didn't exist before, and the write-up inaccurately claims this 'produces the same enumeration as the original' rather than disclosing it as new behavior.

R391.note: Null-coalesces the missing discount to 0 in applyDiscount and null-guards the comparison in isDiscountApplied, matching the stated contract for both the present- and absent-discount cases.
